keyVerseText: The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
rootMeaning: The name Ἰησοῦς (Iēsoûs) is of Hebrew origin, derived from the root word יְהוֹשׁוּעַ (Yᵉhôwshûwaʻ), which means 'Jehovah is salvation.' This etymology reveals that the name carries a profound theological meaning beyond the common English transliteration 'Jesus.' It emphasizes the divine source of salvation, linking the New Testament figure to the Old Testament concept of deliverance embodied in Joshua, the leader who succeeded Moses.
usageInScripture: The word Ἰησοῦς appears 975 times in Scripture, predominantly translated simply as 'Jesus' (830 occurrences). Other translations like 'of Jesus,' 'when Jesus,' and 'to Jesus' show its frequent grammatical variations in context. This consistency highlights the name's central role as the proper noun identifying the Lord Jesus Christ, while also reflecting its use in various syntactical forms that connect Jesus personally and relationally within the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding Ἰησοῦς as 'Jehovah is salvation' is crucial for a Christ-centered faith because it directly points to Jesus' identity as the divine Savior promised throughout Scripture. His name encapsulates the mission of salvation that defines His person and work. This connection to the Old Testament name Joshua enriches the Christian understanding of Jesus as the ultimate leader who brings God's people into their spiritual inheritance. Recognizing the divine origin and meaning of His name strengthens faith in His authority and redemptive power.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 1:1 introduces the genealogy of Jesus Christ, emphasizing Him as 'the son of David, the son of Abraham.' The use of Ἰησοῦς here anchors the Messiah's identity in the fulfillment of God's promises to Israel. The name Jesus in this verse is not merely a label but a declaration that salvation has come in the person of the promised descendant, connecting the Old Testament covenantal history with the New Testament revelation.
